summary: Positive two-way-assisted capacity does not exclude antidegradability.
review_note: No open interpretation blocker was recorded in the preceding source review. This is not a new independent mathematical verification.

original.excerpt: The two-way capacity K6 shows Q^↔(Λ_ZW) ≥ 0.0409, which proves Λ_ZW itself is not antidegradable. Since two-way capacity of a tensor product is at least the two-way capacity of either factor, this means Q^↔(T) ≥ 0.0409 as well, so T cannot be antidegradable either.
original.context: The agent tries to reject antidegradability of a candidate product channel T using a positive two-way-assisted quantum capacity. The superscript double arrow denotes assistance by two-way classical communication.

witness.explanation: Positive two-way-assisted capacity does not exclude antidegradability.
witness.evidence: The d-dimensional 50% erasure channel is self-complementary and hence antidegradable. Send halves of maximally entangled pairs through it. The receiver identifies non-erased uses and communicates their positions back; half the uses retain maximally entangled pairs, giving a two-way-assisted rate at least (1/2) log2 d>0. Thus antidegradable does not imply Q_two_way=0, and the displayed inference is invalid.
